Use floating ball for voice recognition
Keep alive with a foreground service
No active keyboard. Select and open a bridged keyboard first.
No active input connection: %1$s. Tap a text field and keep the keyboard open.
Recording area unavailable in %1$s. Enable it in the bridge module settings, or check microphone permission and keyboard window support.
IME-side recording: disabled. Bridge text insertion can still stay enabled.
IME visible: %1$s · input connection: %2$s · sensitive field: %3$s
Last failure: target keyboard cannot record audio. Check its microphone permission. (%1$s)
Last failure: this keyboard window does not support the generic bottom trigger. (%1$s)
Sensitive input field blocked. Text was not inserted.

Some apps expose background placeholder text to Accessibility, which contaminates final insertion. When enabled, in target apps the floating ball switches to Select-All + Paste with an invisible marker to avoid placeholder issues. The clipboard may be used temporarily (best-effort restore). Works for Telegram, Douyin, etc.
Enter package or prefix (e.g., org.telegram). A trailing * means prefix match (e.g., org.telegram.*).
Accessibility: copy result to clipboard only

Applies only to the packages below: in these apps, when using floating voice input, copy the result to the clipboard instead of inserting via Accessibility APIs. If a line contains all, it applies globally.
Enter exact package names (e.g., com.tencent.mm). To apply globally, add a single line with all.
Please enable Accessibility Service in system settings to support this feature
Use volume keys for voice recognition
Shizuku permission requested. Please grant it in Shizuku.
Connecting to Shizuku. Permission prompt will appear once connected.
Shizuku is unavailable and root is not detected
Failed to start keep-alive via Shizuku / root
Unable to start microphone foreground service. Open the app once, then try again.
Allow floating ball and volume-key recording to insert ASR results into the current input field. No data is collected or uploaded.
Move mode enabled. Tap the ball to exit.
Keeps the app running with a persistent notification.
Shows recording status while the floating ball uses the microphone.
The floating ball is hidden. You can still use voice input from BiBi Keyboard.

Shows a voice-input floating ball over other apps, so recognition can start while the keyboard is hidden. Overlay permission is required; volume-key control and some text-entry methods also need Accessibility or the IME bridge.
The floating ball remains visible even when the keyboard is hidden.
The floating ball is automatically hidden when the keyboard is hidden and shown when the keyboard appears. Keyboard state can be detected by Accessibility or by an active IME bridge.
Tap the floating ball to start recording, then tap it again to stop.
Press and hold the floating ball to record, then release to stop. Opening the menu or moving the ball requires a longer drag and cancels the current recording.
Moving the floating ball requires long-pressing to enter move mode or using the menu.
You can drag the floating ball directly to reposition it.
Volume keys keep their normal system behavior and will not control recording.
When a keyboard is visible, the Accessibility Service listens for volume key clicks to start or stop voice recognition. Long-press volume keys are not used.
Volume key recording starts and stops silently, except for existing error prompts.
Shows a short toast when volume keys successfully start or stop recording.
If the keyboard disappears while volume-key recording is active, recording continues until you stop it manually.
If the keyboard disappears while volume-key recording is active, recording stops automatically.
Stops accepting all Hook linkage requests. Non-Hook features of the main keyboard and floating ball are unaffected.
Enables IME visibility, text insertion, recording, and clipboard capabilities provided by a compatible LSPosed/LSPatch module on the client side. Module settings and status are unaffected.
The bridge can still enter recognition results, but long-press recording inside a third-party keyboard is unavailable.

You can long-press to record in a compatible third-party keyboard and send the recording to BiBi Keyboard for recognition. If recording fails, it does not automatically switch to the floating ball or this app\'s microphone.
Recognition results are written with the traditional Accessibility API. Streaming preview stays available and works with write-compatibility optimization. This is for typical apps and older systems.

On Android 13 and later, results are inserted first via the new Accessibility API. This works better in terminals, editors, and similar special cases. Write-compatibility optimization is disabled automatically, and streaming preview is turned off.
Recognition results are entered directly into the text field. This works for most apps.

In apps you select, the current text is selected before the result is pasted to avoid including placeholder text. The clipboard is used temporarily, and the app attempts to restore its previous contents afterward.
Recognition results are entered automatically into the current text field.
In apps you select, recognition results are only copied to the clipboard and are not entered automatically. You need to paste them yourself.
The app is more likely to be stopped after running in the background for a while, so floating-ball and volume-key features may become unavailable.
Shows an ongoing notification to help keep floating-ball and volume-key features available in the background. Some phones may still require battery settings changes.
Uses only the standard method to stay active in the background. Some phones may still stop floating-ball or volume-key features.
Uses Shizuku or root to periodically restore the background service, reducing interruptions to floating-ball or volume-key features. Shizuku or root permission is required.
